title: Intraclass correlation for inter-rater reliability, ICC(A,1)
summary: Two-way random, absolute-agreement, single-rater ICC with McGraw and Wong's interval, and the consistency ICC beside it.

sizing._why: ICC sample size depends on the number of raters and the ICC to rule out (Walter, Eliasziw and Donner 1998); no catalog form takes them.

pinned_defaults: Model two-way (the same raters rate every subject, raters random), type absolute agreement, unit single rater: ICC(A,1). irr::icc(model = 'twoway', type = 'agreement', unit = 'single').
Interval: McGraw and Wong's F-based one with a Satterthwaite-type df; Python writes irr's formulas out line for line.
_six_iccs: 'The ICC' is six coefficients. Consistency ignores systematic rater offsets: 0.74 against 0.62 for agreement here. With 4 raters the rater variance is poorly estimated, so ICC(A,1) is less precise than ICC(C,1).
